scenes.heading: Catalogs
scenes.subheading: The top level of Unity Catalog
scenes.narration: In Unity Catalog, a catalog is the top-level container that groups schemas and their tables under one governance boundary.

scenes.heading: Why catalogs matter
bullets: Isolate data by team or environment
Set access control at a broad level
scenes.narration: Catalogs let you isolate data by business unit or by environment such as dev and prod. You can grant or deny access at this broad level and have it flow down. Catalogs also complete the three-level namespace of catalog, schema, and table.

scenes.heading: Creating and using a catalog
scenes.narration: This statement creates a finance catalog and grants the finance team the right to use it. Notice the fully qualified name uses catalog, then schema, then table. That three-part naming is how Unity Catalog keeps assets organized and secure.

scenes.text: Use separate catalogs for environments like dev, staging, and prod to keep governance and data cleanly isolated.
scenes.narration: A common best practice is to use separate catalogs for dev, staging, and prod, which keeps governance and data cleanly isolated.
